name: The Content Engine: 12 Solo Founder Prompts
tagline: Turn a single raw idea into a full week of high-converting content across platforms.
metaDescription: Transform one idea into a week of engaging posts. 12 plug-and-play AI prompts designed specifically for busy solo founders and indie makers.
description:
# The Content Engine for Solo Founders

If you are a solo founder wearing every hat in your business, consistency on social media often feels impossible. You have valuable industry insights, but staring at a blank screen trying to format them into engaging posts wastes precious building time. 

This digital toolkit is built specifically for bootstrap founders, indie makers, and solo entrepreneurs who need a reliable system for content creation. It solves the cold-start problem by taking one raw concept—a feature launch, a customer insight, or a daily frustration—and expanding it into a cohesive week-long narrative.

### Why These Prompts Work
Unlike generic AI writing prompts that spit out robotic fluff, these are engineered using specific frameworks like PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solve), Before-After-Bridge, and contrarian storytelling. They force the AI to adopt a natural, human voice that resonates with target buyers without sounding like a corporate press release.

### What You Get
12 meticulously tested, copy-and-paste prompts categorized by format and platform, delivered as a clean Markdown file and Notion database.
includes: 12 structured AI prompts in Markdown format
Notion database template for easy prompt execution
Usage tips and tone-of-voice modifiers for every single prompt
Free lifetime updates as AI models evolve
sampleItems: Take our recent product update regarding faster dashboard load times and rewrite it into a punchy Twitter/X thread using the Before-After-Bridge framework.
Draft a vulnerable, behind-the-scenes LinkedIn post for a solo founder sharing one major mistake made this week while building in public.

items.title: The Contrarian Take
items.body: Act as an experienced indie SaaS founder. Take the conventional industry belief of [INSERT COMMON INDUSTRY ADVICE] and write a short, punchy LinkedIn post arguing the exact opposite. Back up the contrarian stance with one logical reason and a real-world observation. Avoid corporate jargon, keep sentences under 15 words, and end with a question that invites debate from other founders.

items.title: The Thread Expansion
items.body: Take this core idea or milestone: [INSERT IDEA/MILESTONE]. Expand it into a 6-part Twitter thread. Tweet 1 must hook the reader by breaking a common expectation or sharing a surprising metric. Tweets 2 through 5 must deliver actionable, step-by-step insights without fluff. Tweet 6 must summarize the core lesson and include a soft call-to-action to check out my product. Use line breaks strategically.

items.title: The Founder's Diary
items.body: Write a behind-the-scenes update about [INSERT CURRENT CHALLENGE OR WIN]. Frame the narrative as a diary entry from a solo founder working late at night. Focus heavily on the emotional reality—the doubt, the breakthrough, or the customer feedback that changed my mind. Keep the tone authentic, vulnerable, and relatable to other bootstrapped entrepreneurs.

items.title: The Customer Pain Agitator
items.body: Using the PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solve) framework, write a short email newsletter or community post targeting solo founders who struggle with [INSERT TARGET PAIN POINT]. First, clearly state the problem without exaggeration. Next, agitate the problem by describing the hidden costs in lost time and revenue. Finally, introduce our product, [INSERT PRODUCT NAME], as the logical, frictionless fix.

items.title: The Metric Breakdown
items.body: Analyze this raw business metric or milestone: [INSERT METRIC, e.g., $1k MRR or 500 signups]. Write an educational post breaking down exactly how we achieved it step-by-step. Include one thing that didn't work to maintain credibility. Format the output with clear bullet points so fellow bootstrappers can easily replicate the process in their own micro-startups.

items.title: The FAQ Authority Builder
items.body: Take this common customer question: [INSERT FREQUENT QUESTION]. Answer it thoroughly in a LinkedIn post, but structure the answer by first dismantling why the traditional way of solving this problem is broken. Position our product's methodology as the modern, streamlined alternative. Tone should be authoritative, helpful, and concise.

items.title: The Micro-Case Study
items.body: Write a short case study highlighting how a fictional or anonymous solo founder used [INSERT FEATURE OR PRODUCT] to solve [INSERT SPECIFIC PROBLEM]. Structure the post with 'Before', 'The Pivot', and 'After' sections. Emphasize the time saved rather than just the financial ROI, as time is a solo founder's most scarce asset.

items.title: The Prediction Post
items.body: Draft a forward-looking prediction about the future of [INSERT YOUR INDUSTRY/NICHE] over the next 12 months. Explain how solo founders and small teams will outpace large companies in this specific shift. Use strong, decisive language. Avoid hedging phrases like 'it seems' or 'might be'.

items.title: The Resource Roundup
items.body: Create a high-value resource list for solo founders focusing on [INSERT TOPIC, e.g., automated marketing]. List 3 distinct tools, templates, or strategies. For each item, provide a 1-sentence description and a specific tip on how to implement it in under 10 minutes. Naturally mention how our product fits into this workflow at the very end.

items.title: The Feature-to-Benefit Translator
items.body: Take our technical product feature: [INSERT TECHNICAL FEATURE]. Translate it into a relatable founder benefit by answering the question: 'What mundane task does this let me stop doing today?' Write a short, punchy promotional post for X/Twitter focusing entirely on the emotional relief of gaining back free time.

items.title: The Unpopular Opinion
items.body: Write a 3-sentence micro-post for social media stating an unpopular opinion about [INSERT TOPIC, e.g., venture capital vs bootstrapping]. Make the first sentence a bold hook, the second sentence a brief justification, and the third sentence a direct question asking followers if they agree or disagree.

items.title: The Weekly Review Recap
items.body: Summarize a week of solo founding into a 4-bullet point retrospective covering: 1. Biggest win, 2. Hardest roadblock, 3. One metric that moved, 4. Focus for next week. Keep the tone grounded and realistic, avoiding toxic positivity while still showing steady momentum in building the business.
